title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Every screen back on the map
summary: Kotlin Jump 1.42.35 fixes the Screen Flow map on the commonest way to declare routes, a sealed class of objects. A route holding a path parameter was read as an opening brace, so the screens declared after it lost their qualified name and came back as dynamic routes. The JDK sources are also found on a JDK 8 and indexed four times faster.

highlights.title: Sealed route hierarchies read right
highlights.description: A route holding a path parameter was taken for an opening brace, so the screens after it lost their qualified name and drew as dynamic routes.

highlights.title: Route files no longer skipped
highlights.description: The filter that keeps the map from freezing now knows both shapes it must read, the constant and the object hierarchy.

highlights.title: JDK sources found and lighter
highlights.description: A JDK 8 keeps `src.zip` at its root, a runtime without sources is only a fallback, and the scan drops the four fifths nobody opens.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: Braces inside a route string no longer open a block, so a sealed hierarchy keeps the qualified name of every screen.
A file declaring routes as objects is no longer skipped by the map's pre filter.
`src.zip` is looked for at the root as well as under `lib`, which is where a JDK 8 puts it.
`JAVA_HOME` pointing at a runtime without sources no longer ends the search for a JDK.
The JDK scan keeps `java.base` and the modules actually navigated, cutting four fifths of the work.
